subject: Request: Stage-gate fallback/pinning language for SLA during phased deploys
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@finexco.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finexco.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: Stage-gate fallback/pinning language for SLA during phased deploys

Hi Karthik and Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Procurement has a specific ask before we can sign: FinexCo needs clear contract language that explains how you will protect our 99.9% P99 latency commitment while you do model rollouts (canary / A-B).

Specifically: during canary windows we need an explicit mitigation path (automatic fallback to the previous stable variant and the ability to pin traffic to the stable variant if the canary shows regressions). Our security and platform teams want to avoid any customer-visible latency spikes during rollout.

I've attached our SLA requirements for context (finexco-sla-requirements.pdf). The procurement team would like proposed contract text we can share with legal and SRE. Can you send a short, bulletized description of the operational guarantees and an example failure scenario with the exact fallback behavior?

Thanks — if easier, we can take a short call to align.

Best,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, FinexCo
procurement@finexco.com

--Attachment: finexco-sla-requirements.pdf (application/pdf)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@finexco.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 14:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: Stage-gate fallback/pinning language for SLA during phased deploys

Elena — appreciate the clarity and the attachment. High level summary below; I also attached a proposed term doc (proposed-stage-gate-term.docx) you can hand to legal.

Operational guarantees (short):
- Stage-gate rollout: canary traffic capped at 10% for a minimum 24-hour observation window, with automated health checks (latency, error-rate, token-fill) evaluated every 5 minutes.
- Automatic fallback: if the canary's rolling P99 latency exceeds the baseline by >20% for 3 consecutive 5-minute checks (i.e., 15 minutes), traffic is immediately routed back to the pinned stable variant (no manual approval).
- Pinning behavior: Customers may pin a model version for a configurable period (default 72 hours) during which auto-rolls are disabled; pinned versions continue to receive 100% traffic unless unpinned by the customer.
- Transparent SLO exception windows: Rollout windows are treated as predefined operational windows. During active stage-gates, the platform will apply a documented SLO mitigation policy — if automatic fallback occurs, we will not count the transient rollout window against the 99.9% availability SLA provided that the customer has a pinned fallback configured or accepts the automatic re-route.
- Observability & audit: Request/response traces, token-level latency histograms, and rollback events will be written to your audit logs and retained for 90 days.

Example failure scenario (for contract language):
- At 10:10 UTC, a canary at 10% traffic begins to exhibit increased decoding latency.
- By 10:25 UTC, rolling P99 exceeds baseline by 22% across three checks.
- At 10:25 UTC the routing layer engages automatic fallback: remaining in-flight requests on canary are allowed to complete; new traffic is routed to the pinned stable variant.
- A rollback event and incident entry are recorded; a notification is sent to your configured on-call and to the FinexCo procurement contact.

Notes/limits:
- This behavior relies on compatible model variants; fallback to a non-compatible architecture (e.g., different tokenizer) requires a version pin and explicit migration plan.
- If a customer opts out of automatic fallback (rare), the standard SLA applies without mitigation windows and we will discuss credits if any degradation occurs.

I'll loop Monica (SRE/validation lead) to confirm the observability hooks and retention. If that aligns, I can return a single-paragraph clause for procurement. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to iterate.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions (Redwood Inference)
+1 (415) 555-0192

Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@finexco.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Stage-gate fallback/pinning language for SLA during phased deploys

Looping in a quick management note — Karthik's approach looks workable. A couple of asks before we hand this to legal:

1) Credits language: procurement will want a clear formula for any SLA credits tied to post-rollout regressions. Recommend we offer a limited credit only if no automatic fallback was possible (e.g., incompatible variant) and the customer experienced sustained degradation for >1 hour after mitigation attempts.

2) SRE confirmation: Monica, please confirm that the proposed 5-minute checks and 15-minute trigger window map to our current alerting and that the rollback event is automatically inked into the incident log (so FinexCo gets the trace id + timestamp). Also confirm retention (90 days) is available for enterprise customers.

3) Region fallback: should call out that if primary-region capacity is constrained during rollout, we will route to a secondary region in the same geography. That should be acceptable to FinexCo provided egress/latency is documented.

If these items are OK, we can produce a single contractual clause and a short operational appendix (30–40 lines) for procurement to attach to the SOW.

-Lauren
VP, Sales Operations (Redwood Inference)
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@finexco.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finexco.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:34:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: Stage-gate fallback/pinning language for SLA during phased deploys

Thanks — this is very helpful. Procurement reviewed and prefers the automatic fallback + pin-by-default model (customers can opt out but must accept risk). They also want the credits language to be narrow as you suggested.

Can you please: 1) send the single-paragraph contract clause we can paste into our SOW and 2) a one-page appendix describing the alert thresholds and what the audit log will include (timestamps, trace ids, rollback reason)? If you can attach those as Word/PDF and cc procurement, we can move to signature.

If it's easier, we can sign off on the clause and do the operational appendix as a separate deliverable; procurement prefers the clause up front.

Best,
Elena

On acceptance we'll route the DocuSign to your legal contact.

--procurement@finexco.com
